ai.short_summary: The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority.
ai.detailed_summary: In a landmark decision, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) found Myanmar responsible for state-sponsored genocide against its ethnic Muslim Rohingya population, marking the first time a state has been found culpable of genocide by the top UN court. Delivered by ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa at The Hague in the case of The Gambia v. Myanmar under the Genocide Convention, the ruling follows a 2017 crackdown that left at least 10,000 Rohingya dead and forced vast numbers to flee into Bangladesh. The court ordered restitution and reparations, prompting survivors and community members to hail the decision as a historic victory for international justice, while noting that the struggle for real change will be long and hard. Rohingya survivors recounted horrific experiences of rivers running red with blood and burning villages serving as warnings to flee.
ai.significance: This landmark judgment marks the first time the UN's highest court has held a state directly responsible for genocide, establishing a major precedent in international law.
ai.background_ai: The Rohingya are a stateless Muslim minority predominantly residing in Myanmar's Rakhine State, where they have faced systemic discrimination and severe violence for decades. A major military crackdown in 2017 forced over 700,000 Rohingya to flee across the border into Bangladesh, creating a massive refugee crisis centered around Cox's Bazar. The Gambia subsequently brought a historic case against Myanmar at the International Court of Justice alleging violations of the 1948 Genocide Convention.

The judgment was delivered on Thursday in the case of The Gambia v. Myanmar.

ai.detailed_summary: The UN's COP31 climate conference went into overtime on Friday as negotiators from nearly 200 countries struggled to resolve deep divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance. sources.name: Business Recorder
sources.title: PSX: KSE-100 gains over 500 points in first half

ai.short_summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange saw the benchmark KSE-100 Index rise by over 500 points during the first half of Friday's trading session.
ai.detailed_summary: Following a brief dip in the opening minutes of trading, buying interest returned to the Pakistan Stock Exchange on Friday. During the first half of the session, the benchmark KSE-100 Index gained over 500 points. By 12pm, the index reached 177,274.98 points, representing an increase of 502.80 points or 0.28 percent. Positive momentum and buying activity were noted across several major sectors, such as automobile assemblers, cement, oil and gas exploration companies, oil marketing companies, and power generation. Furthermore, heavyweight stocks including HUBCO, OGDC, POL, PPL, MEBL, and NBP traded positively. This followed a recovery on Thursday when investors engaged in value buying.
ai.significance: The market movement demonstrates renewed buying interest and positive momentum across multiple key sectors at the Pakistan Stock Exchange following a recovery session the previous day.
ai.background_ai: The Pakistan Stock Exchange is the primary stock exchange in Pakistan, headquartered in Karachi. It brings together multiple regional exchanges into a single national market entity. The KSE-100 Index serves as its benchmark indicator for market performance.
key_facts: The KSE-100 Index gained over 500 points during the first half of Friday's trading session.
At 12pm, the benchmark index stood at 177,274.98, reflecting an increase of 502.80 points or 0.28%.
Buying was observed in key sectors including automobile assemblers, cement, oil and gas exploration, OMCs, and power generation.
Index-heavy stocks trading in the green included HUBCO, OGDC, POL, PPL, MEBL, and NBP.
On Thursday, the PSX recovered due to investors engaging in value buying.
exam_points: Pakistan Stock Exchange - KSE-100 Index gained over 500 points in the first half of Friday's trading session.
Index value at 12pm - 177,274.98, up 502.80 points or 0.28%.
Sectors experiencing buying - automobile assemblers, cement, oil and gas exploration companies, OMCs, and power generation.
Heavyweight stocks trading in the green - HUBCO, OGDC, POL, PPL, MEBL, and NBP.
exam_background: Pakistan Stock Exchange - Primary stock exchange of Pakistan formed through the integration of Karachi, Lahore, and Islamabad stock exchanges.

ai.short_summary: Pakistan's auto financing and vehicle sales saw continued growth in October alongside rising interest rates.
ai.detailed_summary: Outstanding car loans in Pakistan climbed for the 23rd consecutive month, reaching Rs416.5 billion in October compared to Rs407 billion in September, according to State Bank of Pakistan data. Consumer demand for cars, SUVs, pickups, and vans drove combined sales up to 24,418 units in October, marking a 41 percent year-on-year increase and a 62 percent month-on-month rise. This brought cumulative sales for the first four months of fiscal year 2027 to 74,898 units, up 26 percent year on year. Meanwhile, the central bank increased the interest rate to 12 percent on October 26, though a banker noted that the rate hike's impact on auto financing would only appear in November data.
